answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to wander a private path through a shared atlas of hash-chained computation steps. A unique marble (one-time nonce bound only to that key) seeds the path; intermediate states cannot be shared or precomputed. Peers verify the final trail. An attacker creating N clones must independently generate and fully compute N distinct marble-seeded paths; because the private marble prevents batching or amortization across identities, total compute cost grows linearly with every additional sybil and cannot be parallelized cheaply.
